one_liner: Real crowdworker clicks vs simulated clicks: quantify the sim2real prompting gap that inflates every interactive segmentation benchmark.
problem: Interactive segmentation is evaluated with simulators (click at center of largest error). Real users click by salience, habit, and motor economy; the distribution gap and its score inflation are unmeasured for general annotators.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: replayed real-user click sessions yield measurably worse NoC/IoU curves than simulator evaluation for the same models (inflation >20% in clicks-to-target), and models RANK differently under real clicks - some architectures are robust to human click styles, others are simulator-tuned.
why_important: If rankings flip under real usage, years of interactive-segmentation comparisons need re-reading, and future evaluation must include click-style robustness.
why_possibly_novel: A public real-click corpus with replay evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Collect 2k real click sessions via crowdsourcing on COCO objects, replay against 5 models, compare with simulator curves.
main_risk: Interface design shapes click behavior; use multiple interface variants to bound the effect.

one_liner: Information-per-second of annotation primitives: clicks vs scribbles vs boxes vs verbal corrections, measured properly for once.
problem: Annotation-efficiency papers compare supervision types by count (10 clicks vs 1 box), not by human time and cognitive cost - the actual currency. The efficiency ordering may invert under time-based accounting.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: under wall-clock accounting with real annotators, scribbles dominate clicks for organic shapes and boxes dominate for convex objects (a shape-conditional efficiency map), while the field's per-interaction accounting has promoted clicks beyond their true standing - and optimal interfaces should switch primitives per object geometry.
why_important: Every labeling operation allocates budget by these tradeoffs; a shape-conditional efficiency map is directly actionable industry-wide.
why_possibly_novel: Time-based shape-conditional efficiency measurement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Timed annotation study (N=20) across primitive types and object-shape strata, fit efficiency map, validate model-training outcomes per budget.
main_risk: Annotator skill heterogeneity; use within-subject designs.

one_liner: Unpromptable objects exist: characterize the reachable mask space of frozen interactive models and what lies outside it.
problem: Interactive models are assumed universal - enough clicks reach any mask. But the decoder's output manifold may exclude some masks entirely (certain topologies, textures), making some objects unreachable at ANY click budget.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for frozen interactive segmenters there exist GT masks whose best reachable IoU (under exhaustive prompt search) plateaus below 0.7 (structural unreachability), unreachable objects share identifiable properties (wiry topology, translucency, extreme aspect), and unreachability persists across prompt types - defining the model's true expressivity boundary, distinct from its average behavior.
why_important: Annotation pipelines assume humans+model can always produce GT; unreachable objects silently corrupt datasets built with model assistance.
why_possibly_novel: Reachability analysis of interactive segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Exhaustive/beam prompt search on 1k diverse objects, identify plateau cases, cluster their properties, verify with human super-users.
main_risk: Search may miss exotic prompt combinations; bound claims by search budget honestly.

one_liner: Label order shapes the final model: easy-first vs hard-first annotation curricula produce different models at identical final budgets.
problem: Datasets are annotated in some order (often easy-first), and models are periodically retrained during collection (model-assisted labeling). Whether the ORDER leaves a permanent imprint on the final dataset+model is unexamined.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in model-in-the-loop annotation, easy-first ordering converges to datasets with systematically different error profiles than hard-first (assistance quality compounds: early model errors seed persistent label styles), and the final-model performance difference at identical budgets exceeds typical method deltas - collection order is a hidden hyperparameter of dataset quality.
why_important: Every assisted-labeling operation implicitly chooses an order; knowing the compounding effect would change collection protocols cheaply.
why_possibly_novel: Order-effect quantification in assisted dataset construction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Simulated assisted-labeling runs with order policies on a fully-labeled dataset (labels revealed per policy), compare final model quality and error styles.
main_risk: Simulation fidelity to real human-model interaction; a small real study for anchoring.

one_liner: Verification bias: annotators accept wrong-but-plausible machine masks at high rates, and the accepted errors are systematically correlated with model style.
problem: Verify-and-fix workflows (machine proposes, human approves) are the industry standard, but acceptance decisions under time pressure may pass through model errors that free-drawing annotators would never make - contaminating datasets with model-correlated noise.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: acceptance error rates for plausible-but-wrong proposals exceed free-drawing error rates severalfold for boundary details and small parts, the accepted errors correlate across the dataset (same model style), and models trained on verified data inherit and AMPLIFY these correlated errors - a measurable contamination loop absent from noise-model assumptions (which assume independent noise).
why_important: Correlated label noise breaks the independence assumptions behind noise-robust training; quantifying the loop is prerequisite to fixing dataset factories.
why_possibly_novel: Correlated-contamination quantification of verify-workflows is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Controlled study: same images labeled by verify-vs-draw protocols, measure error correlation structure, train models on each, compare inherited biases.
main_risk: Time-pressure realism in lab studies; partner with a real annotation vendor for ecological validity.

one_liner: Detect the SAM fingerprint: datasets annotated with SAM assistance carry identifiable boundary-style signatures that future models inbreed on.
problem: Post-2023 datasets are increasingly SAM-assisted. If SAM's boundary style (edge-snapping, blob bias, characteristic curvature spectrum) marks these labels, models trained on them converge toward SAM's biases - ecosystem inbreeding that nobody tracks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a classifier distinguishes SAM-assisted from human-drawn masks at high accuracy using boundary micro-statistics (fingerprint exists), the fingerprint's prevalence in recent public datasets is substantial and rising, and models trained on fingerprinted data reproduce SAM's specific failure modes (holes filled, wires broken) even on classes where SAM was never involved - measurable style inheritance.
why_important: Dataset provenance transparency and bias tracking for the foundation-model era; inbreeding could silently homogenize the field's failure modes into single points of failure.
why_possibly_novel: SAM-fingerprint forensics and inheritance measurement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build fingerprint classifier on known SAM/human mask pairs, survey 10 recent datasets, test failure-mode inheritance in models trained on high-fingerprint data.
main_risk: Post-editing by humans blurs fingerprints; classifier must handle mixed provenance.

one_liner: Where should a scribble go? Skeleton vs boundary-following vs freeform strokes have measurably different information gain per pixel drawn.
problem: Scribble supervision treats all strokes equally, but stroke PLACEMENT geometry (medial axis, near-boundary, random) plausibly changes information delivered per unit effort - the placement policy question is unstudied.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for equal stroke length, skeleton-placed scribbles train better region models while near-boundary parallel strokes train better boundary models (a decomposable placement effect), and a mixed policy tuned per class geometry outperforms natural human scribbling by a meaningful margin - placement policy is worth more than scribble quantity within realistic budgets.
why_important: Scribble platforms can guide stroke placement with simple UI nudges; validated policies convert to free accuracy across weak-supervision projects.
why_possibly_novel: Stroke-placement information analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Synthesize placement-controlled scribbles from GT masks, train per policy at matched stroke budgets, decompose gains by region/boundary metrics.
main_risk: Synthetic scribbles idealize human motor behavior; verify with guided-human study.

one_liner: Region-level active learning with real time-cost models: intra-image selection beats whole-image selection once annotation time is measured honestly.
problem: Active learning for segmentation mostly selects whole images, but annotation cost varies enormously within images; region-level selection with realistic time models (travel time, context acquisition, zooming) has never been evaluated under honest cost accounting.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: under measured per-region annotation time models (including the overhead of context re-acquisition when jumping between regions), region-level selection still dominates image-level by >30% Dice-per-hour at practical budgets, but naive per-pixel-uncertainty region selection UNDERPERFORMS image selection because it ignores overhead - cost-model realism determines the ranking of AL strategies.
why_important: AL research optimizes proxy costs; showing rankings flip under real time models forces the field toward deployable protocols.
why_possibly_novel: Overhead-aware regional AL evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Measure annotation time components in a small study, build cost model, re-simulate AL strategy comparison on 3 datasets.
main_risk: Time models vary by tooling; publish the cost model as configurable artifact.

one_liner: Shape predictability determines point-supervision efficiency: one point suffices exactly when class shape entropy is low - fit the law.
problem: Single-point supervision recovers surprising performance for some classes and fails for others. The determining property is presumably how predictable the class's shape is given one point - a measurable quantity nobody has connected.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the fraction of full-mask performance recoverable from single-point supervision per class is predicted (r>0.8) by class shape entropy (variance of shape descriptors across instances), yielding a practical law: measure shape entropy from a handful of masks, predict point-supervision viability before committing to an annotation scheme.
why_important: Converts supervision-scheme selection from trial-and-error into a measurement-driven decision - direct savings for every new dataset.
why_possibly_novel: Shape-entropy-based supervision-efficiency law is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Across 40 classes from COCO/LVIS, train point-supervised models, regress recovered-performance fraction on shape-entropy estimates from 20 masks per class.
main_risk: Context predictability confounds shape predictability; include context-entropy covariate.

one_liner: Expertise routing: measure WHERE expert annotation beats crowd annotation at the pixel level, and route only those pixels to experts.
problem: Datasets choose expert or crowd annotation wholesale, but expertise plausibly matters only in specific regions (ambiguous boundaries, rare structures); the pixel-level expertise premium map is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: expert-vs-crowd label agreement analysis will show the expertise premium concentrates in <20% of pixels (identifiable a priori by ambiguity predictors), and a routing policy sending only those regions to experts achieves expert-level dataset quality at a fraction of expert cost - measurable end-to-end via models trained on routed datasets.
why_important: Expert time is the scarcest resource in specialized domains (medical, scientific imagery); pixel-level routing is the efficient frontier of annotation economics.
why_possibly_novel: Pixel-resolved expertise-premium mapping with routed-dataset validation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Double-annotate (expert+crowd) 500 medical/complex images, map premium regions, test predictor, train models on routed vs pure datasets at matched cost.
main_risk: Premium maps may be domain-specific; replicate across two domains.

one_liner: Optimal correction-frame selection in video annotation: model uncertainty peaks beat uniform keyframes, but the real optimum is drift-onset frames.
problem: Video annotation corrects the tracker at chosen frames; the frame-selection policy (uniform, uncertainty-based, drift-onset-based) determines total cost, but policies have not been compared under matched click budgets.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: correcting at detected drift-onset frames (from self-diagnosis signals) yields better final video masks than uniform or uncertainty-peak selection at equal correction budget, with the advantage growing with video length - because corrections BEFORE error compounding are worth multiples of corrections after.
why_important: Video annotation is the current cost bottleneck for VOS datasets; a validated frame-selection policy compounds savings across the ecosystem.
why_possibly_novel: Drift-onset-timed correction policy evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Simulate correction policies with SAM2 on DAVIS/LVOS at matched budgets, compare final-quality curves; small human study for timing realism.
main_risk: Drift-onset detection quality gates the policy; co-develop with the self-diagnosis idea.

one_liner: The good-enough plateau: humans stop correcting at ~90% quality, leaving systematic residual errors aligned with model biases in every assisted dataset.
problem: Assisted annotation ends when the human judges the mask 'good enough', not when it is correct. The residual errors are thus model-biased (humans fix salient errors, keep model-style subtle ones) - a structured contamination whose form is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: assisted-annotation residuals concentrate in low-salience error types (boundary offsets in blurry regions, small holes) while free-drawn labels distribute errors differently, the residual structure matches the assisting model's bias profile, and datasets can be forensically dated/attributed to their assisting model by residual structure alone.
why_important: Defines the quality ceiling of the assisted-annotation paradigm and provides provenance forensics; also predicts what SECOND-generation models can and cannot learn from such data.
why_possibly_novel: Residual-structure analysis of the good-enough threshold is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Have annotators 'finish' assisted masks, then expert-audit at high zoom; compare residual profiles across assisting models and against free-drawing.
main_risk: Good-enough thresholds vary with pay/incentives; sample multiple annotation economies.

one_liner: Gaze as free dense supervision: eye-tracking during ordinary image inspection carries recoverable segmentation signal.
problem: Wherever humans inspect images professionally (radiology, quality control), gaze data is potentially collectible at zero marginal effort; its information content for segmentation supervision is essentially unquantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: gaze density and scanpath features around objects contain enough localization signal that gaze-weak-supervised models reach a meaningful fraction (>50%) of point-supervised performance without ANY deliberate annotation, and gaze fixation ORDER additionally encodes object saliency structure usable for curriculum construction.
why_important: Free supervision from existing professional workflows would be transformative for domains where deliberate annotation competes with real work (medicine).
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: gaze studies exist in radiology perception research; segmentation-supervision extraction with performance accounting is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use public radiology gaze datasets (e.g. REFLACX-like), derive gaze-based pseudo-labels, train and compare against point-supervised baselines.
main_risk: Gaze concentrates on diagnostic hotspots, not object extents; may supervise detection better than delineation (report both).

one_liner: Language vs clicks for disambiguation: when scenes get crowded, referring expressions become cheaper than pointing - find the crossover.
problem: Disambiguating a target among similar instances can be done by clicking (spatial) or describing ('the third cup from the left') - the interaction-cost crossover between modalities as scene complexity grows is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: measured in time-to-correct-mask, clicking dominates in sparse scenes but language dominates beyond a measurable instance-density threshold (pointing precision degrades with crowding faster than description length grows), and hybrid systems that ROUTE by predicted density beat either modality alone by >20% throughput.
why_important: Multimodal annotation interfaces are buildable today; the routing law tells builders when each modality pays, grounded in measurement rather than fashion.
why_possibly_novel: Modality-crossover measurement for segmentation disambiguation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Timed human study across instance-density ladder with click-only, language-only, and routed interfaces on crowded scenes (shelves, crowds).
main_risk: Language grounding model quality gates the language arm; use the best available grounding models and report sensitivity.

one_liner: Annotation protocol is a stronger treatment than architecture: same images labeled boundary-first vs region-first produce measurably different trained models.
problem: Protocols (labeling order, tool, instructions) are considered logistics, not science. If protocol-induced differences in trained models exceed typical architecture deltas, the field's controlled comparisons are missing a dominant variable.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: training identical architectures on the same images labeled under two professional protocols (boundary-tracing-first vs region-filling-first) produces models whose performance difference on neutral test sets exceeds the median published architecture improvement - protocol choice silently dominates a meaningful fraction of reported progress.
why_important: A provocative, testable claim about what actually drives measured differences in the literature; would force protocol reporting standards.
why_possibly_novel: Protocol-as-treatment controlled experiments are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Commission dual-protocol labeling of 2k images by the same vendor, train matched models, compare deltas against a survey of published architecture gains.
main_risk: Annotation cost of the dual corpus; mitigate with a focused domain (e.g. one driving subset).

one_liner: Negative-space labels for rare classes: marking 'definitely-not-X' regions is cheap and disproportionately valuable for tail-class learning.
problem: All annotation effort goes into positive labels; explicit negatives (this region certainly contains no X) are never collected, though for rare classes the model's main confusion is what ISN'T the class.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for tail classes, a budget split that spends 30% on definitely-not-X region marking (fast, low-cognitive-load) beats 100%-positive budgets by a measurable margin on precision-critical metrics, because rare-class errors are dominated by hard-negative confusion that positives cannot teach - the value of negative space is class-frequency-dependent and predictable.
why_important: A cheap new annotation primitive with a theory of when it pays - immediately testable by any labeling operation struggling with tail precision.
why_possibly_novel: Explicit negative-region annotation economics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On LVIS tail classes, simulate budget splits using existing annotations to synthesize negatives, then run a small real-annotation confirmation.
main_risk: Negatives may be too easy (uninformative regions get marked); guided negative selection needed.

one_liner: Annotator zoom telemetry is a free boundary-uncertainty ground truth: where humans zoom in, ambiguity lives.
problem: Annotation interfaces record zoom/pan behavior that nobody analyzes; zoom-in events plausibly mark exactly the boundary regions annotators find uncertain - a free, behavioral ambiguity signal at dataset scale.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: zoom-event density along boundaries correlates strongly with inter-annotator disagreement (validating telemetry as ambiguity GT), and models calibrated against zoom-density maps achieve boundary-uncertainty quality comparable to expensive multi-annotator supervision - telemetry replaces redundant labeling for uncertainty training.
why_important: Multi-annotator redundancy is the current (expensive) route to ambiguity ground truth; telemetry is already being recorded and discarded industry-wide.
why_possibly_novel: Telemetry-derived ambiguity supervision is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Instrument an annotation tool, collect telemetry on multi-annotated images, validate zoom-disagreement correlation, train uncertainty heads on telemetry.
main_risk: Zoom behavior also reflects object size and tool ergonomics; regression controls required.

one_liner: Let the model ask: binary yes/no questions about parts ('is the strap included?') beat clicks for ambiguity resolution per second of human time.
problem: Interactive segmentation only accepts spatial gestures, but much residual ambiguity is SEMANTIC (include the handle? the shadow? the attached cable?) - resolvable by one binary answer instead of several corrective clicks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: an interaction budget spent on model-generated binary part-inclusion questions resolves granularity/attachment ambiguity faster (in human-seconds to target IoU) than the same budget in clicks, specifically on objects whose ambiguity is compositional rather than boundary-metric - a measurable interaction-modality advantage on a definable object subset.
why_important: Identifies the right interaction primitive per ambiguity TYPE, moving interactive segmentation beyond pure spatial correction toward mixed-initiative dialogue.
why_possibly_novel: Question-generation for segmentation disambiguation with time-based evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Wizard-of-Oz study: humans answer scripted part-questions vs click corrections at matched time budgets on ambiguous objects (bags with straps, tools with cables).
main_risk: Automatic question generation is a hard subproblem; the study establishes value before building it.

one_liner: Correction propagation: one human fix retrieved-and-applied across thousands of images sharing the same systematic model error.
problem: Model errors are systematic (same failure on similar inputs), but human corrections are consumed once. Retrieving past corrections for similar contexts could amortize each fix across the corpus - the amortization factor is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: corrections cluster in feature space (systematic error families), retrieval-based correction transfer (apply the nearest past correction's local transformation) fixes a substantial fraction of same-family errors without new human input, and the human-effort amortization factor exceeds 10x on homogeneous corpora (aerial tiles, pathology slides) - correction reuse is a neglected order-of-magnitude lever.
why_important: Changes annotation economics fundamentally on large homogeneous corpora, which is exactly where annotation costs bite hardest.
why_possibly_novel: Retrieval-based correction propagation for dense labels is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On aerial/pathology corpora, collect corrections, cluster error contexts, measure transfer precision of retrieved fixes vs fresh model predictions.
main_risk: Bad transfers corrupt labels silently; needs conservative confidence gating and audit sampling.

one_liner: Noisy-many vs precise-few for pretraining: fit the exchange rate between mask quantity and mask quality at fixed annotation budget.
problem: A fixed budget buys either many rough masks or few precise ones. The quality-quantity exchange rate for segmentation pretraining/training - and whether it depends on downstream task boundary-sensitivity - has never been mapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on the quality-quantity frontier at matched budget, region-level downstream tasks favor quantity strongly (rough masks nearly free of penalty) while boundary-level tasks favor quality with a sharp threshold effect (below some precision, masks are worse than useless for boundary learning) - two regimes with a measurable phase boundary that should govern annotation-spec decisions.
why_important: The single most common annotation-planning question, currently answered by intuition; a published frontier with the phase boundary would be a standard reference.
why_possibly_novel: Budget-matched quality-quantity frontier mapping is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Degrade GT masks at controlled precision levels, train at matched simulated budgets across quality-quantity mixes, map the frontier for region vs boundary metrics.
main_risk: Synthetic degradation may not mimic real cheap-annotation error structure; anchor with real dual-quality annotations.

one_liner: Multi-view agreement replaces annotation: photos of the same scene from different angles provide free correspondence-based mask supervision.
problem: Multi-view captures (real-estate scans, photogrammetry, casual multi-shots) constrain segmentation geometrically - a mask valid in one view must reproject consistently to others - but this free supervision channel is unexploited for training 2D segmenters.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: cross-view mask-consistency training on unlabeled multi-view corpora (enforcing reprojection agreement via estimated geometry) improves single-view segmentation of view-dependent failure cases (glare, oblique angles, partial occlusion) by a measurable margin over single-view SSL at matched data volume - geometry is a supervisor that photometric SSL cannot replicate.
why_important: Taps enormous existing multi-view corpora (mapping, real estate, e-commerce turntables) as free dense supervision, targeting exactly the failures single views cannot teach.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: multi-view consistency is used in 3D reconstruction; its harvest as 2D segmentation supervision at scale is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use ScanNet/RealEstate-style corpora, add reprojection-consistency objectives to an SSL baseline, evaluate single-view improvements on shifted test sets.
main_risk: Geometry estimation errors inject noise; restrict supervision to high-confidence correspondences.

one_liner: Click order is a cognitive probe: the sequence in which annotators click parts reveals a shared human object-decomposition that models lack.
problem: Multi-click annotation sequences encode which parts humans consider primary, ambiguous, or boundary-critical - a behavioral window into human object structure that is recorded everywhere and studied nowhere.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: click sequences across annotators show strong order regularities (canonical part order per category: face before limbs, body before accessories), the regularities predict which parts models most often mis-segment (late-clicked parts are model-hardest), and sequence-derived part priorities improve error prediction beyond appearance features - human interaction order encodes a difficulty structure models share.
why_important: A zero-cost behavioral dataset for studying object decomposition, with practical use in error prediction and annotation UI design.
why_possibly_novel: Click-order regularity analysis as cognitive/difficulty probe is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Mine click logs from open annotation projects (or collect via crowdsourcing), quantify order regularities, correlate with per-part model error rates.
main_risk: Order reflects UI layout and motor efficiency too; experimental designs must separate these.

one_liner: Give annotators an explicit 'uncertain' brush: does three-state labeling (yes/no/unsure) improve downstream models over forced binary?
problem: Forced-binary interfaces convert annotator uncertainty into silent noise. An explicit unsure-label preserves the information, but whether models trained with it beat models trained on forced-binary labels (at equal annotation time) is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: three-state annotation costs <10% extra time, the unsure-regions reproduce across annotators (they mark signal, not laziness), and excluding-or-downweighting unsure pixels during training improves test performance on the confident-consensus region more than the removed supervision costs - explicit uncertainty capture is annotation-time-positive.
why_important: A minimal interface change with dataset-wide benefits, directly adoptable by every labeling tool if validated.
why_possibly_novel: Controlled three-state protocol evaluation with downstream accounting is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Dual-protocol labeling study (binary vs three-state) on ambiguous-heavy imagery, train matched models, compare on high-confidence test regions.
main_risk: Unsure-label semantics drift between annotators without careful instruction design.

one_liner: Tool fingerprints across public datasets: identify which annotation software made each mask and quantify tool-induced bias in the ecosystem.
problem: Public datasets were annotated with different tools (polygon editors, brushes, assisted systems) whose geometric artifacts (vertex spacing, curvature quantization, snap behaviors) enter the labels - the ecosystem-wide composition and its downstream effects are unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: mask micro-geometry classifies annotation tooling with high accuracy across major datasets, tool composition differs strongly by dataset era and domain, and models trained cross-dataset devote measurable capacity to tool-style translation (probeable as tool-predictive features in the trained weights) - the ecosystem carries a tooling-bias layer nobody accounts for.
why_important: Meta-transparency for the entire benchmark ecosystem, and a concrete confounder to control in cross-dataset studies.
why_possibly_novel: Ecosystem-scale tool forensics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble tool-labeled mask corpora (known-provenance datasets), train fingerprint classifier, survey 15 public datasets, probe trained segmenters for tool-feature encoding.
main_risk: Provenance ground truth for older datasets is scarce; bootstrap from documented cases.

one_liner: The 100-labeled-pixels challenge: map the extreme-low-budget frontier of segmentation to find where each supervision paradigm collapses.
problem: Label-efficiency papers compare at comfortable budgets (1-10% of pixels); the extreme regime (say 100 labeled pixels per class total) has no map, though it reveals which paradigms extract the most information per label bit and where each breaks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at extreme budgets, paradigm rankings invert relative to comfortable budgets (foundation-feature probing dominates fine-tuning; consistency methods collapse entirely below a measurable threshold; point-supervision beats mask-supervision per pixel), producing a budget-vs-paradigm phase map with actionable regime boundaries - the field's efficiency conclusions are budget-regime-specific and do not extrapolate down.
why_important: Scientific applications (rare phenomena, expert-only labels) live in the extreme regime the literature never visits; the phase map is their missing guidance.
why_possibly_novel: Extreme-budget phase mapping is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Budget ladder from 100 to 100k labeled pixels across 5 paradigms on 3 datasets, plot the phase map with collapse thresholds.
main_risk: High variance at tiny budgets demands many seeds; compute cost is real but bounded.
